sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Autonomous Crop Spraying Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi n° 2017-399 du 27 mars 2017 relative à la transparence, à la lutte contre la corruption et à la modernisation de la vie économique, as amended by Ordonnance n° 2021-... and subsequent decrees implementing EU Directive 2015/849 on AML/CFT

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity card of UBO
Certificate of incorporation or equivalent for corporate UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, and beneficial owners against French, EU, UN, OFAC, and other sanctions/PEP lists using automated tools compliant with AML/CFT regulations

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin alphabet; company names must comply with French orthography and grammar rules
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Prohibited: 'banque', 'assurance', 'mutuelle', 'crédit', 'institution financière'; Sensitive: names of public authorities, military terms, requiring prior approval from relevant ministries
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the greffe within 30 days; further recourse to the tribunal de commerce if needed

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for SAS if the registered office is a physical address with professional mail reception services, but must demonstrate economic activity and substance to avoid sham company risks under EU commercial substance rules
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to medium risk of unannounced inspections; primarily document-based verification during incorporation and ongoing compliance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO due diligence and beneficial ownership screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for cross-border AML due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and clearance search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee plus administrative costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office setup and compliance documentation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS), together with Articles R.227-1 et seq. and applicable notarial and registry decrees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Commercial Court in the jurisdiction of the registered office; electronic filing administered through INPI's single portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constatant la constitution de la SAS (Articles of Association) accompanied by the official electronic M0 declaration form and individual attestations of corporate officers and beneficial owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital is imposed for an SAS; capital may be fixed freely. Where capital is subscribed in cash, at least half of the subscribed cash amount must be paid in before filing and held in a blocked (escrow) account with a credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, with the balance payable within five years of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the capital subscribed by each shareholder as set forth in the Articles of Association is hereby accepted; the registered office is fixed at the address indicated in the first article; each appointee named in the annex list is appointed as chair of SAS, general manager and other corporate officers with authority given to file all formation documents; the chair is authorized to execute every declaration, pay fees and taxes, and carry out all formalities until registration is achieved; and all actions already taken in this respect are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Registre National des Entreprises, via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and the RCS search database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online pre-verification of the proposed SAS name against the RCS national register and the INPI trademark database. If an identical or confusingly similar name exists, select an alternative. The name may be optionally reserved through the single portal before drafting the statutes.
required_dossiers: Three alternative proposed company names
Identity copy of the lead founder
Indication of intended registered office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict, promptly file a corrected name or apply to the registry president with evidence of prior use or coexistence; if rejected due to conflicting trademark rights, seek withdrawal or file a preliminary opposition response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signing of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, where a contribution in kind is made, a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) or civil-law notary if real property is contributed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association of the SAS containing mandatory clauses: corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, share subscription table, rights and obligations of shareholders, management powers and decision rules. All founders and participating shareholders must sign the final text; each page is initialled and the signature page is dated. A contribution in kind report and any notarized deed are prepared at this stage.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Lease or ownership title for the proposed registered office
Contribution in kind valuation report if applicable
Certified translation of foreign public documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later queries statutory wording, convene an extraordinary general meeting and adopt amendatory articles, then refile the corrected statutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Cash Capital and Blocked Account Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the SAS in formation. Deposit at least fifty percent of each cash share subscription and obtain an attestation de dépôt de fonds (funds deposit certificate) listing the amount deposited, the subscriber's identity and the statement that funds are blocked until registration.
required_dossiers: Preliminary Articles of Association
KYC forms and identity documents of beneficial owners
Bank account opening form for the SAS in formation
Statement of cash and non-cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the deposit for unresolved KYC or missing signatory authority, complete the due diligence, obtain a corrected power of attorney and re-submit the deposit file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Announcement in an Authorized Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcement journal in the department of the registered office (support d'annonces légales, usually chosen in the department of the siège social).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a statutory formation notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SAS), capital, registered office, corporate purpose and officers. Obtain the attestation de parution with the announcement registration number, which must be submitted with the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final draft of the Articles of Association
List of corporate officers
Amount of share capital
Registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is defective or the journal's certificate is incomplete, republish an amended notice and pay an additional publication fee; the corrected certificate may be used for the filing without waiting beyond ordinary SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with INPI and Examination by the RCS Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI single electronic portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic M0 formation dossier on the official portal. Attach the signed Articles of Association, funds deposit certificate, legal announcement certificate, declaration of beneficial owner and identity documents of officers. Pay filing fees online through the portal. The greffe examines the dossier for legal compliance, urgency, and completeness, then registers the company and issues the Kbis extract with a SIREN number.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association
Funds deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Legal announcement publication certificate
M0 electronic form data module
Identity documents of officers and beneficial owners
Proof of registered office occupation
Power of attorney, if the filing is made by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query, respond within 15 days with additional documents or corrected trans                                                                          lations; if the file is refused, the applicant may file an administrative and judicial appeal before the president of the commercial court pursuant to Article L.123-13 of the French Commercial Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registration is effective, retrieve the Kbis certificate and obtain the SIREN/SIRET numbers. Open the company's operational bank account, order a corporate seal, create statutory corporate registers, and keep the share subscription ledger available at the registered office. Verify that the APE/NAF code corresponds to the ISIC mapped scope of agricultural machinery manufacture.
required_dossiers: Kbis receipt
Registration confirmation from the portal
Corporate seal order form
Statutory registers and share transfer ledger templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains a copying error in company data or legal form, request a free correction from the greffe; if registry data remain inaccurate, file a rectification request with supporting statutory instruments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de l'Aviation Civile (DGAC) – Mission Drones, in coordination with the Direction Générale de l'Alimentation (DGAL) of the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation spéciale pour l'épandage aérien de produits phytopharmaceutiques au moyen de drones agricoles (Special authorization for aerial spray application of plant protection products using agricultural drones), issued under the French Rural and Maritime Fishing Code, together with DGAC certification, where applicable, for the UAS technical class.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – Inspection des Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Likely ICPE Enregistrement regime for manufacturing workshops with surface-treatment, painting or solvent use; a full EIA report may be required if production capacity exceeds fixed thresholds, alternatively a simple déclaration or exemption applies to segregated assembly and testing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits as per the French ministerial order of 2 February 1998 (COD ≤ 125 mg/L; BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L; suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L; pH 5.5–8.5); VOC emissions limited to 150 mg C/m³ for aqueous process exhaust and 110 mg C/m³ for dry exhaust under Directive 2010/75/EU; all hazardous waste storage and routing must conform to ICPE rubrique 2615 and be traceable via registered disposal documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: commission de sécurité visitation and final fire certificate for occupied premises, including emergency exits, fire alarms, extinguishers and hazardous storage compartments; structural load inspection required for any elevated test platform, drone hangar or landing pad; occupational clearance: DREETS workplace inspection including electrical installation verification, first aid provisioning, noise exposure assessment, and compliance with the Labour Code on working conditions and medical surveillance of operators.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), the French national tax authority under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; primary portals: impots.gouv.fr, guichet-entreprises.gouv.fr, and the unified registration portal le-guichet-unique.inpi.fr operated by INPI; customs and excise matters for export verification are under the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, tax identity is obtained ex lege at incorporation: (1) file statutory articles of association and the appointed president via the INPI 'Guichet unique' portal within 30 days; (2) publish the incorporation notice in a legal gazette (journal d'annonces légales); (3) INSEE automatically issues the SIREN (9-digit entity number) and SIRET (establishment number); (4) DGFiP automatically assigns the corporate income tax account (n° fiscal) and the VAT intra-Community identification number (format FR plus 2-digit DGFiP key plus SIREN, 13 characters total); no separate VAT registration certificate is required in France, and no minimum capital is imposed for SAS formation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not maintain a US-style check-the-box regime. Relevant elections for an SAS include: (1) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under CGI Art. 223A, available to a parent holding at least 95% of eligible French subsidiaries, requiring a joint 5-year irrevocable election; (2) parent-subsidiary participation exemption (régime mère-fille) under CGI Art. 145/216, yielding 95% dividend exemption; (3) the option for the reduced corporate income tax rate on small and medium enterprise profits; (4) election of the export-oriented 0% VAT treatment under CGI Art. 262; and (5) ATAD hybrid mismatch compliance declarations for cross-border hybrid arrangements (CGI Art. 209 VII-X), filed on the annual corporate return with marginal anti-avoidance elections where the French payer or French investor is the counterparty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: French-established traders benefit from the franchise en base small-business exemption (CGI Art. 293 B) up to EUR 91,900 annual turnover for goods and EUR 36,300 for services (2025 thresholds); intra-EU B2C distance sales are registered in France via OSS until EUR 10,000 annual cross-border turnover; non-established foreign suppliers must obtain French VAT registration from the first taxable euro and generally must appoint a DGFiP-approved fiscal representative; exports of goods outside the EU are zero-rated and do not trigger registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France implements a mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting clearance model rather than an Italian-style live fiscal stamping: all B2B e-invoices must use structured semantic formats (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) and be transmitted through the free Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a DGFiP-accredited private platform (PDP) with certified REST/API interfaces; transactional data is cleared to DGFiP simultaneously with issuance, and B2C payment data is e-reported; the reform timetable requires all taxable persons to be able to receive compliant e-invoices from 1 September 2026 and to issue them from 1 September 2027 for large and mid-cap companies and from 1 September 2028 for small and micro companies; no digital fiscal stamp or QR clearance code is affixed to French invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under CGI Art. 262-I for goods physically exported outside the European Union customs territory and under the place-of-supply rules (CGI Art. 259-1 and 262-II) for services directly connected to export goods or supplied to non-EU B2B customers; the exporter must evidence removal of goods from EU territory within 90 days of dispatch, supported by a valid DAU export entry processed through the DELTA-X electronic customs system; intra-EU dispatches are exempt under CGI Art. 262-0 with submission of the EC Sales List and the French déclaration d'échanges de biens (DEB); refund of accumulated input VAT is claimed via the dème de remboursement de crédit de TVA (form 3519 or monthly periodic refund procedure) supported by export invoices, DAU receipts, transport documentation, and bank credit evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - DAU (Document Administratif Unique) processed via DELTA-X
Transport evidence: Bill of Lading, House Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note proving exit from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice bearing the zero-rated export VAT exoneration reference under CGI Art. 262
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/TT credit advice evidencing actual receipt of foreign export proceeds
Export licensing records for dual-use or civil UAV/drone-specific controlled goods where applicable under DGDDI strategic goods regulation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exporters must retain substantiation for at least 6 years; customs verification may extend retrospectively up to 3 years and tax authorities up to 6 years in fraud cases. Where zero-rating is invalidated (false export declaration, fictitious consignee, missing exit proof, or non-repatriation of proceeds within the reference window), DGFiP will reassess French VAT at 20% with 0.20% monthly late interest and may apply an 80% bad-faith or fraudulent-misrepresentation penalty under CGI Art. 1729; DGDDI may separately impose customs penalties under Code des Douanes Art. 414-426, including confiscation of the goods, fines up to twice the value of the fraud, and imprisonment up to 3 years for smuggling or misdeclaration; refunds previously granted may be clawed back with the same penalties, and serious cases may be referred to the French tax fraud prosecution authorities (Parquet National Financier) for criminal trial.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully convertible regime for both capital and current accounts. The Euro faces no capital controls or prior approval requirements for cross-border transfers. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are unrestricted provided standard corporate tax compliance, beneficial ownership declarations, and AML reporting obligations are met.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds applies under French law. Export receipts are declared for statistical purposes via Banque de France reporting mechanisms where applicable, but conversion occurs at market rates without quotas or prescribed ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs due to French Payment Services Directive compliance and strict AML oversight. Local licensed banks are preferred for cross-border operations involving export licenses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote KYC and digital onboarding is permitted for French SAS entities under French banking regulations, but directors and beneficial owners may be required to attend physical interviews or provide video verification for high-risk sectors such as AgTech exports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity involving autonomous drones and agricultural spraying equipment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of manufacturing license, export authorization, detailed business plan, proof of beneficial ownership, and audited financial statements to demonstrate legitimate commercial purpose

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires source of funds documentation, shareholder resolutions, and alignment with corporate charter. All transactions subject to ongoing KYC monitoring.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. For agricultural exports, integration with platforms like TradeIX or local French banking networks for efficient clearing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for SMEs on first EUR 38,120 taxable profit; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% up to EUR 400,000 qualifying costs; territoriality relief for foreign PE profits under applicable DTA; optional group tax consolidation regime for French subsidiaries.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory expiry); annual utilisation is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the surplus taxable income above that amount. A one-year carryback of up to EUR 1,000,000 is available under limited SME conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French corporate income tax return: Formulaire n° 2065-SD (CERFA n° 15616) together with annexes, principally n° 2051 to 2059-AS. Mandatory e-filing through the 'Espace Professionnel' on impots.gouv.fr using the EDI (Échanges de Données Informatisés) application.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year financial period ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the third working day following 1 May. For an off-calendar financial year, filing is due by the third month after the close of the financial year. If the statutory deadline falls on a non-working day, the one-day rule is postponed to the next working day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the French SAS, SIREN number, RCS commercial registration number, NAF/APE code corresponding to ISIC 2821, registered office address, share capital, and tax identification reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder: identify the French permanent establishment or branch separately, provide the French tax registration number attributed to the PE, and furnish the foreign tax residence identification used for treaty purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the taxable result after accounting income adjustments, tax-deductible provisions, depreciation restatements, loss carryovers, group integration adjustments, and applicable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only French-source profit attributable to the PE in accordance with Article 209 CGI and the relevant DTA permanent establishment provisions. Attach the reconciliation of the French PE's separate accounts and exclude non-French income unless the treaty permits French taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex 2051, 'Détermination du résultat fiscal' / loss carryforward section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of net operating losses brought forward, exhausted ordinary losses, and the annual deductible amount respecting the statutory cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers may deduct only losses economically attributable to the French PE; losses recognized outside France or in a foreign head office may not reduce French taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, tax credits and reduced rates section (CIR / CII)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of research tax credit, innovation tax credit, foreign tax credits, and other itemized credits affecting the final corporate income tax position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident manufacturers carrying out eligible agricultural drone R&D in France through a French PE may claim CIR/CII on French-incurred expenditures; attach the specific credit annexes and substantiate technical, legal, and financial operation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% increase in tax due if no formal demand is issued, rising to 40% after a formal demand, and to 80% for concealed activity or fraudulent manoeuvres. In addition, late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month on the unpaid tax. Failure to file may also result in a fixed administrative penalty and heightened tax audit exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax on dividends distributed by a French SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders outside any applicable treaty or directive. The rate is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying EU/EEA parent holding at least 5% of the SAS for at least two years, and may be reduced under France's income tax treaties to rates commonly ranging from 0% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the nonresident beneficial owner must obtain a certificate of tax residence issued by the foreign competent authority (usually presented on French Form 5000 or the equivalent EU certificate) and submit it to the French Service des Impôts des Entreprises before the distribution date. The claimant must also provide evidence of legal ownership, holding period, beneficial ownership status, and substance sufficient to avoid the French 'abus de droit' and the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive abuse provisions. For EU parent exemption, the parent must further document the 5% shareholding condition and submit the residence certificate to the French withholding agent to avoid the domestic 25% levy.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law applies a 33.33% withholding tax on gross patent, trademark, or know-how royalties paid by a French debtor to non-resident recipients, unless reduced under an applicable DTA, generally to 0%, 5%, or 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and Form 5000 residence certification. Interest on ordinary arm's-length debt owed by a French company to non-resident creditors is not subject to French domestic withholding tax; the treaty rate is normally 0%, though specific anti-tax-haven rules may impose a 30% WHT in respect of payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File obligations arise for French entities and permanent establishments forming part of a multinational group where the French entity has more than 100 employees and has an annual turnover or total gross assets exceeding EUR 50 million. Country-by-Country Report filing applies to groups with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more. Agricultural drone companies below these thresholds are still required to prepare contemporaneous arm's-length evidence sufficient to satisfy French tax audit standards.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not administer a standalone Economic Substance Regulation in the Gulf Cooperation Council sense, but economic substance is a binding precondition for treaty benefits, EU directive benefits, and transfer-pricing recognition. The French 'abus de droit' doctrine, ATAD Article 6 general anti-abuse provisions, and the substance prerequisites of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive require the French SAS to have actual management, decision-making, operational staff, fixed assets, and real drone assembly or R&D functions in France, not merely a registered office shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of agricultural drone revenues, use of fictitious supplier invoices, falsification of export documentation, creation of artificial foreign entities to divert French profits, or intentional suppression of the taxable base in the annual n° 2065-SD filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of undeclared tax with a 40% bad-faith penalty or an 80% fraudulent-manoeuvres penalty, plus late-payment interest. Criminal prosecution may lead to a fine of EUR 500,000, or EUR 1,000,000 where aggravated, and imprisonment of up to five years, or seven years where the offence is committed by an organized group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the French SAS is used to disguise the tax fraud of its directors or beneficial owner. Directors risk civil restitution for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties, travel bans, asset freezes, seizure of passports, disqualification from managing a French company, and imprisonment for complicity in fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Inadequate Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling agricultural drone sprayers, spare parts, or IP royalties to a related foreign distributor at a non-arm's-length price, reducing French profitability; failure to prepare or produce the Local File and Master File on a timely subsequent demand by the tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority may recharacterize transactions, adjust the French taxable profit, apply the arm's-length principle under Articles 57 and 238A CGI, and impose late-payment interest plus an administrative penalty of up to 40% for serious misrepresentation or 80% where abusive. Non-production of documentation can independently attract penalty and audit-cost burdens.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve transfer-pricing manipulation without economic substance may be assessed personally for taxes and sanctions if they benefited from the pricing scheme. In criminal cases, directors who made false statements to the administration may face personal fines and imprisonment, and the same sanctions as tax-fraud offenders where the mispricing is part of a fraudulent concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company and Abuse of Treaty / EU Directive Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the French SAS solely as a shell to hold drone-related IP licences, CIR tax credit claims, or foreign dividends without any real operational staff, office, or decision-making in France, or routing profits to zero-tax jurisdictions through a non-genuine entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the domestic law tax treaty benefit and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption; application of the French anti-abuse doctrine to recharacterize the whole arrangement; 40% or 80% penalties, interest, and potential nullity of the corporate entity if fictitious. In certain cases, charges may include unlawful tax benefit and fraudulent registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be found personally liable for the French tax reassessment and penalties where the shell company is a vehicle for abuse. Sanctions include a French management ban (interdiction de gérer) of up to 15 years, asset confiscation, travel restrictions, and personal criminal fines for intentionally organizing the sham arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Export Control, and Financial Sanctions Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Financing the drone export trade through opaque nominee bank accounts, failure to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner of the SAS, cash or wire payments from sanctioned end-users, failure to obtain the required dual-use or drone export licences from DGAC/DGA, or breaching asset-freeze obligations in the target payment rail operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code, criminal fines of up to EUR 375,000 and imprisonment of up to five years for money laundering, confiscation of the export proceeds and aircraft, withdrawal of the manufacturer/operator licence, and liquidation of the French entity where the permits are invalid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally liable for AML and sanctions breaches involving the SAS. The corporate veil may be pierced where the structure is used for international money laundering or sanctions evasion; consequences include personal asset confiscation, travel bans, passport denial or revocation, prohibition from banking operations, and imprisonment.
